title: Tombak (zarb) goblet drum rhythms
summary: The tombak, also called zarb, is the goblet drum of Iran, turned from mulberry or walnut wood and often inlaid with fine mosaic. The player sits with it across the lap and plays with the fingers and palm in quick, graceful patterns: the deep Tom in the centre, Bak with the fingers near the edge, Rik with a roll of the four fingertips.
howToPlay: Three places on the head are lit: the centre for Tom, the inner ring for Bak and the outer ring for Rik. The hoop is the Pelang, a rim tap.
A ring closes on the place to strike. Strike it as the ring closes.
The patterns are in six, two groups of three. Start with the six-eight pulse, then try the roll figure.
rules: A stroke on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra strokes cost points.
Each pattern is played twice through.
Patterns are simplified teaching figures in the style of the tradition, not transcriptions.
heritageNote: A tombak player adds tiny rolls and decorations around a simple skeleton. The six-beat patterns are the pulse of classical and folk music alike.
